subject.title: [Feature]: Support to edit system prompt template

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class user-editable override contract for OpenClaw-owned system prompt sections such as Safety, Tool Call Style, OpenClaw Control, and Self-Update?
rationale: This changes model-facing safety guidance and prompt precedence, while current main intentionally exposes narrower provider, hook, channel, bootstrap, and SDK prompt surfaces; automation cannot choose the permanent product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve Scoped Text Section Overrides
options.body: Add a narrow named-section override model with explicit edit authority, precedence, security docs, text-only behavior, prompt-cache rules, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep Core Sections Fixed
options.body: Reject user-editable core sections and document provider overlays, channel prompts, plugin hooks, and bootstrap files as the supported customization paths.

options.title: Defer To Narrower Prompt Work
options.body: Let identity-line, config-rules, include, and hook-replacement work proceed independently while leaving broad Safety/template editing unresolved here.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Text Section Overrides
recommendation.body: Add a narrow named-section override model with explicit edit authority, precedence, security docs, text-only behavior, prompt-cache rules, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent history on provider-owned prompt contributions and the OpenClaw-owned prompt boundary this decision would change.
